messages.subject: Re: Status of DOQTL genome scan model options
messages.subject_clean: Status of DOQTL genome scan model options
messages.body_plain:
If you call scan1() using the 36-state probabilities as output by calc_genoprob(), you'll be fitting the full model.

If you first convert the 36-state probabilities to allele dosages, using genoprob_to_alleleprob(), and then use those 8-state probabilities in scan1(), you'll be fitting the additive allele model.

karl

messages.subject_clean: Time to event analysis in DO mice
messages.body_plain:
It maybe depends on whether the 10% that didn't reach the event are just censored or whether they were basically cured and would never have shown the event.

I guess I would start by just plugging in the maximum observed time. But you could also explore treating them as properly censored values, say in a Cox proportional hazards model. Or do the analysis of the quantitative trait among the mice with observed event values, and then the binary trait (event observed or not), along the lines of Broman 2003 https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/12663553 The overall sample size will have a big effect on things. Are we talking about 10% of 300 or of 600?

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Kinship matrix values
messages.body_plain:
The kinship coefficient for two individuals is: select an allele at random from each of the individual, what’s the probability the two alleles are identical by descent? For a non-inbred individual, this is 1/2. With a bit of inbreeding, it’ll be a bit > 1/2.

See https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_relationship#Kinship_coefficient

grav dataset is for RIL. totally inbred so kinship coefficient with self is 1.

iron data is F2. 1/2 chance homozygous, 1/2 chance het. ibd probability for random alleles is 1 if homozygous and 1/2 if het, so self-self kinship coefficient for individuals will be 1/2 x 1 + 1/2 x 1/2 = 3/4. actual amount of homozygosity will vary, and so realized self-self kinship coefficient will also vary: more homozygous == large value on the diagonal.

karl

messages.subject: Re: plot_coef
messages.body_plain:
The column names in do.hap$founder_geno don't get used.

You can control the allele labels in a couple of ways. You can provide them with the argument legend_lab, like so:

strains <- c("ACI", "BN", "BUF", "F344", "M520", "MR", "WN",  "WKY")
plot_coef(co, pmap, legend="topleft", legend_lab=strains)

Or if you provide colors with col, if that vector has names, they are used.

my_colors <- CCcolors
names(my_colors) <- strains
plot_coef(co, pmap, legend="topleft", col=my_colors)

The colum names in the output of scan1coef() are taken from the names in the genotype or allele probabilities that are provided, and those are taken from do.hap$alleles, which are generally single letters so that the labels for genotypes become two-letter strings rather than something unwieldy like "ACIACI" or "ACIBN".

The order of the founder strains in the allele probabilities is as in do.hap$founder_geno, so you could take the names from there:

my_colors <- CCcolors
names(my_colors) <- rownames( do.hap$founder_geno[[1]] )
plot_coef(co, pmap, legend="topleft", col=my_colors)

karl
